interest: This file offers a compelling window into the post-World War II transition of American intelligence agencies, illustrating the operational handoff from the Office of Strategic Services / Strategic Services Unit (SSU) to the fledgling Central Intelligence Group (CIG) and the Department of State. It reveals how minor administrative and liaison staff stranded in wartime Europe—specifically a Japanese national who worked for the South Manchuria Railway and the Japanese Military Attaché in occupied Paris—became the focus of international intelligence coordination and early Cold War anxieties regarding communist infiltration. The collection also documents the complex bureaucratic and logistical mechanics of postwar repatriation, showing multilateral coordination between U.S. occupation authorities (SCAP and USPOLAD), the postwar Japanese government's Central Liaison Office, the French Foreign Office and French Mission in Japan, and French colonial authorities in Indochina.
overview: This file (decimal file 894.20251) documents the intelligence screening, surveillance, and eventual repatriation of Kikue Kato (Kikué Kato), a Japanese national residing in Paris from 1937 to 1947 who was suspected of wartime intelligence and propaganda activities. Having served as a secretary for the South Manchuria Railway's Paris office and the Japanese Military Attaché, as well as an alleged wartime liaison with Japanese groups in Switzerland, Kato sought to return to Japan in late 1946. Her visa applications prompted investigation by the Strategic Services Unit (SSU) and the Central Intelligence Group (CIG) due to potential espionage concerns and suspected ties between her Russian companion, Pierre Tchelebi, and French and Soviet communist groups—suspicions that subsequent inquiries largely discounted. The documents record the inter-agency and diplomatic correspondence among the State Department, SSU/CIG, the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) and U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo, the Japanese Government, and the French Mission in Japan, tracing Kato's journey from Paris through Marseilles and Saigon to her arrival in Japan aboard the S.S. General Gordon in August 1947.

subfiles.about: GSA withdrawal notice for a classified document removed from file 894.20251/3-2245.
subfiles.summary: This withdrawal sheet (GSA Form 7117) records that an item designated 894.20251/3-2245, dated March 22, 1945, was removed from the file during archival review on April 20, 1976. The withdrawn record was correspondence from Reba to Dina and was restricted under National Archives guidelines because it contained security-classified intelligence methods and agent information.
subfiles.title: National Archives Document Withdrawal Notice for File 894.20251/3-2245

subfiles.about: SSU intelligence report detailing Kikue Kato's wartime activities in Paris and suspected communist connections, transmitted to the State Department.
subfiles.from: Lester C. Houck, Chief, Dissemination Branch, SO, Strategic Services Unit
subfiles.summary: Lester C. Houck of the Strategic Services Unit (SSU) transmits report DB-1982 to Jack D. Neal of the State Department regarding Kikue Kato, a Japanese national in Paris seeking repatriation. The report outlines Kato's prewar and wartime connections to the South Manchuria Railway and the Japanese Military Attaché's office, as well as intelligence liaison work between Paris and Switzerland. It notes her receipt of a French exit visa, pending application for a Chinese transit visa, and an alleged romantic relationship with a Russian named 'Monsieur Pierre,' who was tentatively identified as an operative linked to the Union des Patriotes Soviétiques and the French Communist Party.
subfiles.title: SSU Intelligence Report DB-1982 on Kikue Kato with Transmittal Memorandum
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State

subfiles.about: State Department airgram transmitting SSU intelligence on Kikue Kato to the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary of State Dean Acheson transmits Outgoing Airgram A-173 to the United States Political Adviser to SCAP in Tokyo, quoting in full the SSU intelligence report concerning Kikue Kato. The airgram alerts occupation authorities that Kato, who worked for Japanese intelligence and propaganda organs in Paris during the war, is attempting to return to Japan. It provides details regarding her background, visa applications, and potential political ties to communist networks via her companion 'Monsieur Pierre' to assist occupation officials in monitoring her case.
subfiles.title: State Department Airgram A-173 to USPOLAD Tokyo Concerning Kikue Kato
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo airgram forwarding a SCAP G-2 biographical profile of Kikue Kato to the State Department.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser, Tokyo (George Atcheson Jr.)
subfiles.summary: In response to the State Department's Airgram A-173, the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo submits Airgram A-15 containing a biographical sketch of Kikue Kato compiled by GHQ SCAP's G-2 Section. The sketch documents her birth, family background, education at Futaba Girls High School, and previous employment with the Foreign Ministry's Trade Bureau, the French-operated Kobe Imperial Oxygen Company, and the Nichifutsu Kaikan. It also confirms she received a passport in September 1937 to travel to France via Suez aboard the André Lebon as a nurse for the children of a French shipping company manager.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Airgram A-15 Transmitting SCAP G-2 Biographical Sketch of Kikue Kato

subfiles.about: CIG report clearing Kikue Kato's companion of communist ties and reporting French assistance for her repatriation.
subfiles.from: Lester C. Houck, Chief, Source Control Branch, SO, Central Intelligence Group
subfiles.summary: Lester C. Houck of the Central Intelligence Group (CIG) transmits report DB-3295 to Jack D. Neal, updating the State Department on the status of Kikue Kato. The report indicates that the French Foreign Office has assisted Kato in resolving travel difficulties and that Pacific Allied Control authorities have no objection to her return if transportation is secured. Furthermore, Paris investigations established that her companion is Pierre Tchelebi, refuting earlier suspicions that he was the communist activist 'Monsieur Pierre' associated with Soviet front groups.
subfiles.title: CIG Intelligence Report DB-3295 on Kikue Kato with Transmittal Memorandum
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo despatch reporting Japanese Government and French Mission communications regarding Kato's transit through Saigon.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (H. Earle Russell for George Atcheson Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1147 from the U.S. Political Adviser in Tokyo informs the Secretary of State of arrangements regarding the repatriation of Kikue Kato. The mission reports that the Japanese Government requested assistance on behalf of her father after Kato embarked from Marseilles for Saigon, French Indochina, in late March 1947. USPOLAD forwarded the request to the local French Mission without comment and encloses the French Mission's confirmation that Kato reached Saigon and will board the next available vessel for Japan.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Despatch No. 1147 on the Repatriation of Kikue Kato

subfiles.about: Memorandum from the French Mission in Japan confirming Kato's arrival in Saigon and scheduled embarkation for Japan.
subfiles.from: French Mission in Japan (Mission Française au Japon)
subfiles.summary: This memorandum (No. 187) from the French Mission in Japan to the Diplomatic Section of SCAP responds to SCAP's inquiry of May 5 concerning the repatriation of Kikue Kato. The Mission states that the High Commissioner for France in Indochina has confirmed Kato's arrival in Saigon. It assures SCAP that she will be placed on the first available Japan-bound vessel.
subfiles.title: French Mission in Japan Memorandum No. 187 on Kikue Kato's Repatriation
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Diplomatic Section

subfiles.about: USPOLAD Tokyo despatch confirming Kikue Kato's repatriation to Japan aboard the S.S. General Gordon.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (Counselor of Mission / H. Earle Russell)
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 1278 from the Counselor of Mission at USPOLAD Tokyo provides final confirmation regarding Kikue Kato's repatriation. Citing a note dated September 10, 1947, from the Japanese Central Liaison Office, the despatch confirms that Kato was successfully repatriated to Japan on August 27, 1947, traveling aboard the S.S. General Gordon via Hong Kong.
subfiles.title: USPOLAD Tokyo Despatch No. 1278 on Kikue Kato's Return to Japan
